name: ArtifactsBench
description: ArtifactsBench is a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on interactive visual artifacts. It contains 1,825 executable queries across nine domains and uses an automated, multimodal evaluation pipeline that executes artifacts in a sandbox, captures three staged screenshots, and scores outputs with checklist-guided MLLM referees.
creator: Tencent Hunyuan Team
citeAs: ArtifactsBench: Bridging the Visual-Interactive Gap in LLM Code Generation Evaluation
rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was curated through a multi-stage pipeline combining expert sourcing with LLM generation and refinement. Candidates were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query generation from screenshots. Automated filters removed incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items. Two-stage de-duplication and contamination control used MinHash plus semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS, followed by screenshot perceptual hashing. Experts rewrote prompts for clarity, completeness, and executability; LLM rewriting added diverse styles; humans verified. Solvability was validated with candidate solutions from multiple families, and underspecified or brittle tasks were revised or removed.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Document analysis, Others
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Candidate tasks were sourced from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query generation from screenshots.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Tasks were filtered, de-duplicated, re-authored or discarded if flagged, rewritten by experts and LLMs, verified by humans, calibrated for difficulty post hoc using aggregated performance of 30+ models, and tagged into sub-categories by a lightweight classifier with human spot-checks.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automated filters dropped incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items. De-duplication used MinHash and semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS, plus screenshot perceptual hashing for visually near-identical artifacts. Prompts were rewritten for clarity, completeness, and executability, and tasks solved only by brittle hacks were revised or removed.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each query was paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities. Checklists were drafted by LLMs and then human-refined for specificity and screenability. A 10% manually curated seed anchored calibration and achieved Cohen's kappa >= 0.8 among annotators; the seed was reused as few-shot references to keep difficulty high and rubrics consistent. Sub-categories were tagged by a lightweight classifier with human spot-checks. Human validation of the evaluation used a double-blind study on 280 queries and 6 models, scored independently by multiple front-end engineers, with the final human ground-truth score taken as the median of individual annotators' ratings.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Playwright with headless Chromium was used in the execution harness to render artifacts and capture screenshots for evaluation.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Checklist calibration used a 10% manually curated seed and achieved Cohen's kappa >= 0.8 among annotators. Human validation measured pairwise consistency rate (Pair ACC) between automated referees and human experts on 280 queries and 6 models. The final human ground-truth score was the median of individual annotators' ratings. Cross-judge robustness was analyzed between Gemini-2.5-Pro and Qwen2.5-VL-72B, and version stability was checked by comparing Gemini-2.5-Pro-Preview-0506 with stable Gemini-2.5-Pro.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Multiple engineers with extensive front-end development experience; annotators in the human study were front-end engineers.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini-2.5-Pro, Qwen2.5-VL-72B, Hunyuan-Turbos, Gemini-2.5-Pro for query classification, lightweight classifier for sub-category tagging
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark is open-sourced at https://artifactsbenchmark.github.io. The paper states that dataset specs, checklist templates, evaluation scripts, and referee settings are released. It also notes version stability analysis for replacing deprecated Gemini-2.5-Pro-Preview-0506 with stable Gemini-2.5-Pro, but no explicit update schedule or deprecation policy for the dataset itself is provided.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The query quality filtering prompt explicitly aims to select privacy-free queries and avoid sensitive personal information such as phone numbers, addresses, or other identifiable details.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to provide the community with a scalable and accurate tool to accelerate the development of user-centric generative models and to evaluate qualities central to user experience in modern applications.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that multimodal LLM referees can suffer from hallucination, prompt sensitivity, limited awareness of engineering/code quality, version drift, and potential cognitive biases in interpreting long-horizon interaction logic and dynamic visual feedback. It also notes that referee evaluation criteria may diverge from human judgments.
rai:dataLimitations: The current methodology evaluates dynamic behavior using a sequence of screenshots at fixed intervals, which may not fully capture highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions such as multi-step workflows or nuanced game physics. The benchmark focuses on the final artifact generated in a single turn and does not assess iterative agentic refinement, self-debugging, or multi-turn development processes.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on interactive visual artifact generation. It is used to assess model performance across visual fidelity, interactive correctness, and code quality, compare over 30 LLMs, validate automated referees against human experts, and provide fine-grained diagnostics and leaderboards.
